title: Union-find form of the exchange argument
statement: Let $\mathit{uf}\colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ be a union-find state whose classes coincide with the reachability classes of an edge list $\mathit{base}$: for all nodes $a,b$ one has $\mathit{uf}(a) = \mathit{uf}(b)$ if and only if $a$ and $b$ are joined by a path through the edges of $\mathit{base}$. Let $S$ be a further list of weighted edges, and let $e$ be a weighted edge with endpoints $u$ and $v$ such that merging every edge of $S$ into $\mathit{uf}$ places $u$ and $v$ in a common component, while $\mathit{uf}$ itself keeps them in distinct components. Then there is an edge $f \in S$ for which the state obtained by first merging $u$ with $v$ and then merging all edges of $S$ other than $f$ induces the same partition of the nodes as the state obtained by merging all edges of $S$ into $\mathit{uf}$.
hypotheses_covered: uf's classes are exactly the reachability classes of base
merging all of S into uf identifies the endpoints of e
uf keeps the endpoints of e in distinct classes
replaced:
Let $\mathit{uf}$ be a union--find state whose classes are exactly the reachability
classes of an edge list $\mathit{base}$, i.e.\ $\mathit{uf}\,a = \mathit{uf}\,b$ iff
$a$ and $b$ are reachable in $\mathit{base}$. If merging all edges of $S$ into
$\mathit{uf}$ identifies $e.u$ and $e.v$ while $\mathit{uf}$ itself keeps them apart,
then there is an edge $f \in S$ such that
$(\mathit{uf}.\mathtt{merge}\,e.u\,e.v).\mathtt{mergeAll}\,(S \setminus \{f\})$
induces the same partition as $\mathit{uf}.\mathtt{mergeAll}\,S$.
